newsitem.title: UK: Watson & Philip makes profit warning.
newsitem.headline: Watson & Philip makes profit warning.

text.p: Food distributor and retailer Watson & Philip Plc said on Monday it expected profits before property and exceptional items to be at the lower end of market expectations.
Watson and Philip said profits would be at the lower end of forecasts principally because of a timing delay in building the W. & P. Foodservice new business in line with structure costs.
It said there would also be exceptional losses estimated at 1.3 million sterling primarily related to the disposal of redundant properties.
"We continue to be confident that next year and in future years our strategy and plans will show strong profit growth," said the company in a statement.
October 27 is the financial year for Watson and Philip.
Watson and Philip finance director George Leckie told Reuters that the lower end of market expectations for profits was around about 20 million stg. He said the range was 18.5 million to 22 million.
Final results are due on January 31.
It reported pre-tax profit of 18.5 million stg earlier this year for the year to October 29, 1995.
Watson and Philip said its major subsidiary Alldays Stores has traded well and broadly in line with expectations despite lower than anticipated lottery revenues.

It also announced that Alldays has signed an agreement with Total Oil, owned by Total SA, which will see a major expansion of its retail partnership with Total and will span an initial five year period covering Total's directly operated service stations.
